validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline exists and is mothballed. The sheet owner is Gazprom International Projects LLC, but the cited news sources name Nord Stream 2 AG as the project company, with Gazprom as sole shareholder, and a German subsidiary for the 54 km German section. A person should decide whether the row records Nord Stream 2 AG as owner.

verifications.note: capacity to deliver 55 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas per year
Total capacity: 55 bcm of natural gas per year

fills.researcher_notes: Deutsche Welle (Nov 2020) says the pipeline is designed to deliver up to 55 billion cubic meters per year. Enerdata (2020) and Interfax-Ukraine (2021) give the same 55 billion cubic meters a year. The Espoo report for Nord Stream 2 also says the system will deliver 55 billion cubic metres of gas per year. Deutsche Welle (Nov 2020) says the pipeline is designed to deliver up to 55 billion cubic meters per year. Enerdata (2020) and Interfax-Ukraine (2021) give the same 55 billion cubic meters a year. The project fact sheet also says total capacity is 55 bcm per year.

Deutsche Welle (Nov 2020), the Clean Energy Wire fact sheet and a Washington Post explainer all give 1,230 km for the pipeline. The Nord Stream 2 project fact sheet (2018, read as a 2022 Wayback copy) and a New Europe article of July 2019 (read as a 2022 Wayback copy) both say about 1,230 km.

verifications.note: Overall costs including financing costs: around 9.5 billion euros

fills.researcher_notes: Deutsche Welle (2017), Radio Free Europe (2019), Clean Energy Wire (citing Nord Stream 2 AG) and the Washington Post all give a project cost of 9.5 billion euros. This is the pre-construction estimate. A later Radio Free Europe item gives about 11 billion US dollars, which is a currency conversion of the same estimate. The project fact sheet says overall costs including financing are around 9.5 billion euros.

The Clean Energy Wire fact sheet says Reuters reported in March 2023 that the pipelines were set to be sealed and mothballed, with no plans to repair them, and that chances of operation are very low. The Euractiv copy of the Reuters report says the same. Kommersant of 28 Nov 2022 says Gazprom will mothball the compressor stations that fed Nord Stream and Nord Stream 2, and that both pipelines were blown up and are not working. The first two are Reuters-based, so they count as one source.

verifications.note: owned by Gazprom international projects LLC
owned by Russian state-owned gas giant Gazprom

fills.researcher_notes: Radio Free Europe (Jan 2022) says the pipeline operator, Swiss-based Nord Stream 2 AG, is owned by Gazprom. The Washington Post and Deutsche Welle (2017) call Nord Stream 2 AG the project company and say Gazprom is its sole shareholder. The lowest-level holder named in the sources is therefore Nord Stream 2 AG. The sheet names Gazprom International Projects LLC, which none of the cited pages mention. In January 2022 Nord Stream 2 AG set up a German subsidiary, Gas for Europe GmbH, to own and operate the 54 km German section. The company site (2022 Wayback copy) says Nord Stream 2 AG is the project company, owned by Gazprom International Projects LLC, a Gazprom subsidiary. Reuters of March 2022 (Wayback copy) says Nord Stream 2 AG is owned by Gazprom.

verifications.note: each pipeline will have an internal diameter of 1,153 mm (48 inches)

fills.researcher_notes: The Estonian environment ministry copy of the Espoo report for Nord Stream 2 (read as a 2021 Wayback copy; the live envir.ee link does not load) says each pipeline will have an internal diameter of 1,153 mm (48 inches). The sheet value is 1153 mm. The Nord Stream 2 fact sheet on the company site was not readable.
no wiki citation states a 2022 start. The Clean Energy Wire fact sheet says construction was completed in 2021 and the pipeline never began operation; not searched further this pass.
